claim: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is a heterogeneous group of bone marrow stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis and cytopenias, most commonly anemia.
source: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is a heterogeneous group of bone marrow stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis and cytopenias, most commonly anemia.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about MDS that draws from established scientific consensus and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Red cell transfusion therapy for anemia in MDS results in iron overload, correlating with reduced overall survival.
source: Red cell transfusion therapy for anemia in MDS results in iron overload, correlating with reduced overall survival.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research demonstrating the correlation between transfusion-related iron overload and survival outcomes.

claim: NUP98-HOXD13 transgenic mice are a highly penetrant well-established MDS mouse model.
source: We evaluate underlying iron-related pathophysiology and the effect of iron chelation using deferiprone on erythropoiesis in NUP98-HOXD13 transgenic mice, a highly penetrant well-established MDS mouse model.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior publications establishing this mouse model.

claim: Deferiprone-treatment reversed the iron overload phenotype with aberrant erythropoiesis in NHD13 mice.
source: Our results characterize an iron overload phenotype with aberrant erythropoiesis in these mice which was reversed by deferiprone-treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Serum erythropoietin levels decreased in deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
source: Serum erythropoietin levels decreased while erythroblast erythropoietin receptor expression increased in deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Erythroblast erythropoietin receptor expression increased in deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
source: Serum erythropoietin levels decreased while erythroblast erythropoietin receptor expression increased in deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Expression of iron chaperones Pcbp1 and Ncoa4 was normalized in late-stage erythroblasts from deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
source: We demonstrate, for the first time, normalized expression of the iron chaperones Pcbp1 and Ncoa4 and increased ferritin stores in late-stage erythroblasts from deferiprone-treated MDS mice, evidence of aberrant iron trafficking in MDS erythroblasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Ferritin stores increased in late-stage erythroblasts from deferiprone-treated MDS mice.
source: We demonstrate, for the first time, normalized expression of the iron chaperones Pcbp1 and Ncoa4 and increased ferritin stores in late-stage erythroblasts from deferiprone-treated MDS mice, evidence of aberrant iron trafficking in MDS erythroblasts.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Erythroblast ferritin is increased in response to deferiprone, correlating with decreased erythroblast ROS.
source: Importantly, erythroblast ferritin is increased in response to deferiprone, correlating with decreased erythroblast ROS.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Genes involved in iron uptake, sensing, and trafficking are increased in expression in stem and progenitor cells from MDS patients.
source: Finally, we confirmed increased expression of genes involved in iron uptake, sensing, and trafficking in stem and progenitor cells from MDS patients.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by analysis of patient data shown in Figure 9.

claim: In the United States, MDS affects approximately 100,000 people with a median age of 65 years at diagnosis.
source: In the United States, MDS affects approximately 100,000 people with a median age of 65 years at diagnosis and an incidence of 40/100,000 per year thereafter (Rollison et al., 2008; Goldberg et al., 2010).
evidence: This epidemiological statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: MDS has an incidence of 40/100,000 per year after age 65.
source: In the United States, MDS affects approximately 100,000 people with a median age of 65 years at diagnosis and an incidence of 40/100,000 per year thereafter (Rollison et al., 2008; Goldberg et al., 2010).
evidence: This epidemiological statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Low-risk MDS patients account for approximately two-thirds of all MDS patients.
source: Low-risk MDS patients account for approximately two-thirds of all MDS patients with 30–50% requiring regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions (Dayyani et al., 2010; Kröger, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: 30-50% of low-risk MDS patients require regular red blood cell transfusions.
source: Low-risk MDS patients account for approximately two-thirds of all MDS patients with 30–50% requiring regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions (Dayyani et al., 2010; Kröger, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A correlation between iron overload and reduced survival has been demonstrated mostly by retrospective studies.
source: A correlation between iron overload and reduced survival has been demonstrated mostly by retrospective studies (Malcovati et al., 2006; Malcovati et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: RBC transfusion-dependence correlates strongly with decreased survival in MDS patients.
source: RBC transfusion-dependence correlates strongly with decreased survival in MDS patients (Garcia-Manero et al., 2008; Malcovati et al., 2005)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: MDS patients with elevated serum ferritin have significantly fewer Burst Forming Units (BFU-Es) but normal Granulocyte Macrophage Colony Forming Units (CFU-GM).
source: MDS patients with elevated serum ferritin have significantly fewer Burst Forming Units (BFU-Es) but normal Granulocyte Macrophage Colony Forming Units (CFU-GM) (Hartmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Iron overload has been shown to inhibit BFU-E colony formation and erythroblast differentiation in both murine and human hematopoietic progenitors in vitro.
source: Iron overload has been shown to inhibit BFU-E colony formation and erythroblast differentiation in both murine and human hematopoietic progenitors in vitro (Taoka et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Cells exposed to excess iron exhibit dysplastic changes with increased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and decreased expression of anti-apoptotic genes.
source: Finally, cells exposed to excess iron exhibit dysplastic changes with increased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and decreased expression of anti-apoptotic genes (Taoka et al., 2012)
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The addition of iron to MDS patients' peripheral blood mononuclear cells resulted in increased ROS and DNA damage, triggering apoptosis.
source: the addition of iron to MDS patients' peripheral blood mononuclear cells resulted in increased ROS and DNA damage, triggering apoptosis (Fibach and Rachmilewitz, 2012; Pan et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Iron chelation is associated with improved hemoglobin (Hb) and reduced RBC transfusion requirements in some patients.
source: Iron chelation is associated with improved hemoglobin (Hb) and reduced RBC transfusion requirements in some patients (Oliva et al., 2010; Badawi et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The TELESTO trial demonstrated prolonged event-free survival in iron overloaded lower risk MDS patients treated with iron chelation (i.e. deferasirox).
source: Most recently, the TELESTO trial demonstrated prolonged event-free survival in iron overloaded lower risk MDS patients treated with iron chelation (i.e. deferasirox) (Angelucci et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: No clear improvement in Hb or reduction in RBC transfusions and no effect on overall survival was observed in deferasirox-treated MDS patients in the TELESTO trial.
source: However, no clear improvement in Hb or reduction in RBC transfusions and no effect on overall survival was observed in deferasirox-treated MDS patients.
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to the TELESTO trial results.

claim: Deferiprone (DFP) has a lower iron binding affinity relative to transferrin.
source: Alternatively, unlike other commercially available iron chelators, deferiprone (DFP) has a lower iron binding affinity relative to transferrin (Sohn et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The DFP iron chelating effect enables iron transfer from parenchymal cells to increase transferrin saturation which results in increase hepcidin expression in the liver in response to systemic iron.
source: As a consequence, the DFP iron chelating effect enables iron transfer from parenchymal cells to increase transferrin saturation which results in increase hepcidin expression in the liver in response to systemic iron (Schmidt et al., 2015; Casu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NHD13 mice replicate alterations in gene expression identified in MDS patients.
source: We use NHD13 mice because they replicate alterations in gene expression identified in MDS patients and are the most commonly used transgenic mouse models of MDS (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: NHD13 mice are characterized by abortive erythroblast maturation and consequent ineffective erythropoiesis.
source: More specifically, NHD13 mice are characterized by abortive erythroblast maturation and consequent ineffective erythropoiesis and are, therefore, of target interest in our search for a mechanistic understanding of ineffective erythropoiesis to target its amelioration (Lin et al., 2005; Slape et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NHD13 mice have been successfully used in pre-clinical studies to investigate the effects of an activin receptor II ligand trap on reversing ineffective erythropoiesis in MDS mice.
source: Lastly, NHD13 mice have been successfully used in pre-clinical studies to investigate the effects of an activin receptor II ligand trap on reversing ineffective erythropoiesis in MDS mice (Suragani et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior research.

evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Table 1.
